text:
monica-support: Customer reporting intermittent 503s + high tail latency (~2.5s) on POST /v1/generate. They sent a redacted curl and gave request_id: abc1234def. Happened ~2026-03-12T14:22:11Z. Can someone lookup server logs for that request_id?

alex-eng: On it. Can you paste the exact curl they used (redact API key) and the region/endpoint they hit? Also whether they used streaming.

monica-support: Pasting redacted curl from customer:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Client-Region: us-east-1" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1b","input":"Hello","stream":true}'
```
They confirmed streaming=true. They included response header x-request-id: abc1234def.

kai-sre: Quick Kibana query I ran: `request_id:"abc1234def" OR json.request_id:"abc1234def" OR trace.id:"abc1234def"` within a 30m window around 2026-03-12T14:22:11Z. Found runtime logs showing repeated `kv-cache-miss` entries and a downstream S3 read latency spike (~1.6s) right before the 503. No OOMs.

kai-sre: Grep if you prefer raw: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime --since=3h | rg "abc1234def" -n -C3` — that shows the same pattern.

monica-support: Thanks. Can you paste the exact log lines (redact internal IPs)? I want to send a concise snippet to the customer. Also what is our log retention window? Customer might be worried about missing traces.

kai-sre: Log retention for this cluster is 21 days. If the event is older than that we can't recover server-side logs; will need a debug bundle from the customer. For this request_id the logs are still present. Pasting sanitized lines:
```
[2026-03-12T14:22:11.421Z] runtime-xyz abc1234def INFO incoming request, model=redwood-1b, stream=true
[2026-03-12T14:22:12.103Z] runtime-xyz abc1234def WARN kv-cache-miss key=user-prefix-42
[2026-03-12T14:22:13.789Z] runtime-xyz abc1234def ERROR downstream-s3 read latency=1620ms url=/kv/shard/..
[2026-03-12T14:22:14.134Z] runtime-xyz abc1234def ERROR request failed status=503 err="downstream timeout"
```

ops-bot: If you need a support bundle, run: `support-bundle collect --request-id abc1234def --include-logs --include-traces --output /tmp/support-abc1234def.tar.gz` and ask the customer to upload the bundle to the secure support upload. See https://redwood.internal/support/bundles for instructions.

customer-rep: Customer reports they saw the client-side reconnects and got partial chunks then an abrupt 503. They can repro with the curl above but want to avoid sending full logs. They asked whether this is on our side or theirs. :thinking_face:

alex-eng: Root cause looks like downstream S3 latency causing the runtime to hit our internal timeout path and return 503. Two follow-ups: 1) ask customer to reproduce with `curl -v` so we can confirm response headers and timing; 2) ask if they can try without streaming to see if that changes behavior.

monica-support: Sent customer a short checklist: 1) run `curl -v` (attach response headers and timings, keep API key redacted but include x-request-id) 2) if possible try `{"stream":false}` 3) if they can run support-bundle command (we'll accept sanitized bundle).

kai-sre: If customer won't send bundle and the logs age out, we can only provide high-level summary. For urgent P1s we can request an infra pull of raw objectstore metrics (requires approvals). For now we have the log lines; I'll open a short incident note on /incidents and set severity P2.

monica-support: Customer will try `curl -v` and follow up in ~1h. Marking thread awaiting-customer. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alex-eng: If they repro, ask them to include `-H "X-Request-ID: abc1234def"` in their client so we can correlate. Also ask them to include `--trace-time` output if they can.

ops-bot: Logged action: ticket #SUP-4821 assigned to monica-support, priority=P2, linked thread_ts=1768456789.

monica-support: Noted. Will update once customer provides curl -v output.
